A few small tips, as I was once a major traffic renegade and actually studied traffic law in multiple east coast states:

  • NC is a bit backwards; NC courts still have not taken judicial notice of Radar/Lidar, which means that the 'officer's visual estimation of speed' is the only thing the courts will need to find you guilty
  • However, officers are still required to be trained in visual estimation, and this includes periodical refresher courses. As a quick and dirty rule-of-thumb, if the officer who pulled you over has no Radar/Lidar in/on his vehicle, then he isn't trained.
  • NC, being very backward, is missing a lot of statutes that other states have (e.g. statute of limitations on infractions), which leaves you free to import them from other states (I recommend NY, VT, and FL, all of which have SoL of varying lengths).
  • If you continue your case even once, you implicitly waive your right to a speedy trial, and can't complain if they repeatedly continue your case back (which they will likely do simply to fuck with you).

And finally: NEVER HIRE A BUDGET LAWYER!!!! They will charge you a fee (typically $100-$200) to accept a plea deal that the DA will offer you for free if you simply show up on your court hearing date. These usually come out of a schedule, which he will read off to you, and will sound something like this:

you: [show up in court]

[roll call etc.]

[head DA will tell everyone to form a line if you would like to talk to the prosecutor/DA (same thing)]

you: [waits your turn]

DA: let's see, [fumbling though a bunch of dockets] we have a 90 in a 70. [looks at chart] The best I can offer you is 9 over.

you, if you're wise: I'll take that, then.
